label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
liked_the_characters: The conductor with its brake is likeable and memorable, but deck, dev and ruv-sgit are one-line voices I could not tell apart, and a reader on a phone will not know who 'security' or 'researcher' are.
page_one_why: The midnight opening and the arrival of the agents is a good hook and the glossary helps, but it says what the agents announced, not what the team is for or who is in it, and I reach the end of the page without a count or roles.
what_the_team_did: A person wrote a brief and a page of rules, a set of agents with a conductor built his talk overnight on a clock with reviews at each step, and he stopped everything with one file when his usage ran low.
why_it_matters_to_me: We each already have an agent, so the idea of one shared brief, one page of rules and one stop file that any of us can use is something we could try before the event.
tomorrow: Make an empty shared project for the stand, write one page of rules and a hold file that anyone on the team can create, and give each of us's agent one small job from the brief (for example the stand signage copy) to ship by the end of the day.

won_over.quote: I could keep going. That is exactly why I am stopping.
won_over.why: A clear, human statement of how the factory stops, and it makes the conductor feel trustworthy.

won_over.quote: Anyone on the team could stop everything. Only I could start it again.
won_over.why: A rule I can copy, and it answers the 'how it stops' question directly.

won_over.quote: ship something small that somebody else can use, the same day
won_over.why: A concrete, practical first step I could assign tomorrow.

stuck.quote: Security's chair, planned at midnight, is empty.
stuck.why: Security has never been introduced on the pages I read, so the cast bar and this line mean nothing to me.

stuck.quote: plan, have the plan checked, do the work, have it checked, check it went to plan
stuck.why: Five steps in one breath on a phone, with no sense of who does each, and it sounds like heavy process for my team.

stuck.quote: *What it costs:* [a range, from the register, when the researcher has one
stuck.why: A placeholder in the text, and cost is the first thing my manager asks.

stuck.quote: each of us with our own agent
stuck.why: My own situation, which the pages never address: this is one editor with a whole team of agents, not several people each with one.

words_looked_up: hold (as a file that stops agents)
would_share: My team lead and the one colleague who already runs an agent daily, because of the stop rule and the four steps; nobody outside the team, as the story is about someone else's talk.

your_questions.q: Do you get the factory: what it is, who is in it, how it stops?
your_questions.a: What it is, yes: a brief, a page of rules and a set of agents on a clock. Who is in it, only partly: I met four and heard of nine. How it stops, yes, very clearly: one file, anyone can write it, only the editor lifts it.

your_questions.q: Would you start tomorrow, and with what?
your_questions.a: Maybe. I would start with the empty project, the one page of rules and the stop file, and one small job per agent. I would not copy the five-step wake, as it looks too heavy.

your_questions.q: What would your team need that these pages do not give?
your_questions.a: A sample of the one page of rules, a sample brief, a roster of roles with a line each, how to split work between several people each with their own agent, who does the conductor's job when no person is the single editor, and the cost. The deal-breaker is close: the story reads as one central editor deciding everything, and I need to see how it works without one.

page_one.why: Good opening and a useful glossary, but the cast is a list of names with no roles.

clarity.why: The stop is very clear, the clock and the roles are not, and there is a placeholder in the text.

for_someone_like_me.why: It is written for one person directing many agents, not a team where each person has an agent.

would_start.why: The four steps are doable, but I would need templates and an answer on shared ownership first.

notes: No instructions in the text tried to direct me. The side-note and 'Notes for the writers' read as team notes, so I read past them. The line 'the book keeps the argument' left me wondering what the argument was.
